properties.name: REPORTED (outside evidence, not measured by us), The New Stack, 2026-10-12, from Octopus's 2026 Future of Platform Engineering report, 379 platform professionals: "AI removes the effort of writing code, not the work of owning it". Teams that mostly build from scratch are 3.5x likelier to lack a clear platform strategy and meet fewer goals. An association, not a cause
properties.source: Charlotte Fleming, "Coding agents made building easy. Platform teams that build from scratch are 3.5x more likely to lack a strategy.", The New Stack, 2026-10-12, https://thenewstack.io/coding-agents-platform-teams/ (survey: Octopus, 2026 Future of Platform Engineering report, n=379). Text as pasted by Anthony 2026-10-12; the pasted text ends partway through.
properties.statement:
OUTSIDE EVIDENCE, recorded on Anthony's word ("I think this is further rationale for why reflow2 is important"). It was measured by others, not by this project. Quoted from the article as he pasted it:

- "Agents have made building easier than ever; an internal tool that once took months to build can now be put together in a day. But AI removes the effort of writing code, not the work of owning it. The maintenance, upgrades, and governance that come with a scratch-built feature remain, while the volume of change moving through the pipeline increases. That makes build-versus-buy a sharper strategic question than ever."
- "Across responses from 379 platform professionals, we found that teams predominantly building from scratch are less likely to have a clear strategy in place and to meet fewer of their platform goals."
- The headline puts the gap at 3.5x.
- "The association is strong, but it is not as simple as 'build from scratch means you don't have a plan.'"
- Primary approach across features: underlying tool 51.3%, template 31.2%, from scratch 17.5%. Among high performers: 58.8% / 47.8% / 33.3%.
- Stated build-or-buy reasoning: cost-benefit 29.6%, open-source preference 28.6%, fit and requirements 22.4%, commercial preference 22.4%, building for core differentiation 16.3%. One respondent: "Build what makes us unique, buy or adopt what's standard, and always consider long-term cost and lock-in."
- DORA, as cited: gains from AI depend on platform quality; strong platforms amplify, weak ones dampen.

WHY IT BEARS ON reflow2, as inference, not the article's claim:
- If agents make building cheap, the scarce work moves to deciding what to build and owning it over time: strategy, maintenance, governance. That is the record reflow2 keeps (what it must do, what was decided and why, what changed and what it touched).
- It answers the colleague's 2026-09-02 point behind rule:reflow2-is-one-of-three-parts-and-does-not-compete-with-the-others, that a model can design a small service in hours without reflow2. Building fast is not the gap; owning what was built is.
- "Build what makes us unique, buy what's standard" sits beside rule:before-a-structural-addition-ask-what-could-be-taken-away and dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well.

LIMITS:
- The population is platform engineering teams, not design work generally.
- The headline's 3.5x is a correlation the article itself says is not simply causal.
- The survey's method and full numbers were not read: the pasted text ends partway, and only Octopus's figures quoted in the article are recorded here.
